walkthroughs.body_html:
Area of Study 3: Music for Media — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area of Study 3: Music for Media brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area of Study 3: Music for Media.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the function of the bridge in a pop song?
options: It is the same as the chorus.
ii to V.
To provide contrast before the final chorus, often by changing melody, key, or texture.
It is the very first section.

mcqs.q: Which chords form a plagal cadence?
options: Any sequence of notes a composer chooses.
IV to I (the 'amen' cadence).
V to I.
ii to V.

mcqs.q: What is a tone row in serial music?
options: A row of notes played together as a chord.
ii to V.
Any sequence of notes a composer chooses.
An ordered series of all 12 chromatic pitches, used as the basis of a piece.
